result.summary: Took the PREFERRED path: deterministically forced the TOCTOU race rather than falling back to a spec correction. Read lib/letflow/definitions.ex's activate/2 in full (run_activate_transaction/4, activate_draft/2) and confirmed the exact race window: (1) SELECT...FOR UPDATE locks only the target row, (2) an UPDATE deprecates any prior ACTIVE row sharing the name, (3) an UPDATE sets the target row ACTIVE, (4) COMMIT. The race requires BOTH tasks' step-2 to complete (finding nothing, since both fixture rows start DRAFT) BEFORE EITHER task's step-3 commits -- only then do the two step-3 UPDATEs genuinely fight over the same uq_active_definition partial-unique-index key. activate/2's only production extension point (service_scope_validator) fires too early (before step 2, not between 2 and 3) to serve as a rendezvous, and adding a new test-only hook inside activate_draft/2 itself was rejected as disproportionate surgery on a security-relevant transaction for a need only this one test has. Instead used Ecto's own built-in, already-present [:letflow, :repo, :query] telemetry event (confirmed by reading deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql.ex's log/5 -- emitted synchronously in the querying process right after each query completes, before the caller's code proceeds to the next statement) as the rendezvous: a :telemetry.attach/4 handler pauses each task's process (via a plain `receive`) the first time it observes that task's SECOND process_definitions-sourced query (i.e. right after its deprecate-step, right before its self-activate-step). Once both tasks signal they are paused there, releasing both guarantees the race. Zero changes to lib/letflow/definitions.ex or any other production file. Rewrote test/letflow/definitions/store_test.exs's 'Regression -- activate/2 cross-row TOCTOU' describe block with this mechanism (test renamed to '...deterministically forces the race, never a double-ACTIVE state') and updated its assertions to require EXACTLY one {:ok, %{already_active: false}} and EXACTLY one {:error, {:transaction_failed, _reason}} (previously only an either/or match), since the synchronization now guarantees both outcomes occur every run, not just one of them optionally. Rewrote test/specs/REQ-030.md's 'Regression' section: added an explicit rework note naming the prior No Speculation violation and its root cause (an unsynchronized transaction is usually fast enough that one task finishes before the other starts, landing in the safe branch), described the telemetry-rendezvous mechanism and why the two alternatives (existing hook, new production hook) were rejected, and replaced the single unverified 'did trigger the race' sentence with a citation of this run's actual reproduction evidence. VERIFICATION PERFORMED (not claimed): ran `MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors` clean (0 warnings). Ran the fixed TOCTOU test in isolation across 18 independent seeds (1-8, 11-20) -- 18/18 passed. Directly inspected the mix test debug query log for two of those runs (seed 42, seed 99) and confirmed a real Postgres 'QUERY ERROR' on the self-activate 'UPDATE ... WHERE id = $3 AND status = ''draft''' statement followed by a real 'rollback' -- an actual unique-violation, not an inference. Ran the full test/letflow/definitions/store_test.exs + test/letflow/definitions_test.exs suite 4 additional times (seeds 7, 101, 202, 555) after a clean forced recompile -- all 4 report 'Result: 40 passed', matching the pre-rework count exactly (no regression, no new/removed test cases).
